summary: The bill amends the Social Security Act to add Medicare coverage and payment rules for services furnished by qualified acupuncturists (licensed or certified practitioners), effective 270 days after enactment.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends Medicare (title XVIII of the Social Security Act) to add coverage for qualified acupuncturist services. This directly expands the scope of a major federal entitlement program, increasing federal outlays for healthcare services that were previously uncovered. No offsetting spending reductions are included.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue measures.

The legislation expands Medicare coverage to include services provided by licensed acupuncturists, broadening the scope of a public insurance program. This aligns with expanding public coverage rather than shifting toward private or market-based alternatives.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

No provisions address reproductive health services, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense programs, or national security spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy standards.
By expanding Medicare benefits for seniors, the bill enlarges a key federal entitlement program that functions as part of the social safety net for older Americans.

No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No provisions address policing, sentencing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill increases federal spending through expanded Medicare coverage without any accompanying revenue increases or spending cuts elsewhere, thereby contributing to larger deficits.
